clue.text: Expel from European country after leader's replaced

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and this phrase says it is swapped for another one

parts.note: something from Denmark is Danish

explanation.surface: A government deports someone back to their homeland once a new head of state takes over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after leader's replaced' swaps the first letter of DANISH; the clue does not name the new letter, so the crossers and definition have to supply the B.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to send them away by decree, a synonym of expelling them.

clue.text: Writing style reporter outlawed, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words here trade their first consonants

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, often a jobbing one
banned means prohibited, outlawed

explanation.surface: A banned journalist's handwriting is described by the famously muddled Oxford don.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the H and B of HACK BANNED gives BACK HANNED, which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Backhand is handwriting that slopes to the left, a recognised style of penmanship.

clue.text: On way up, organise drink for young child

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means a word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to run something is to organise it
a sling is a gin-based cocktail, as in Singapore Sling

explanation.surface: Climbing the stairs, a parent fixes a drink for a toddler.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursling is an infant still being nursed, so a young child.

clue.text: Building in swish Edinburgh

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of the words swish Edinburgh

explanation.surface: A building is found in a smart part of Scotland's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is a simple outbuilding, an example of a building.

clue.text: Fast food in Paris? No!

parts.note: a French dish of snails, famously slow creatures, so anything but fast food

explanation.surface: Someone denies that Paris serves up quick takeaway meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast food' suggests burgers; the 'No!' says this French delicacy is the slowest food imaginable, being snails.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for snail, used for snails cooked as a delicacy in garlic butter.

clue.text: US farmer, potential buyer, welcomes article about credit

indicators.note: a word that welcomes others takes them inside itself

parts.note: a shopper is someone who may buy
A is the indefinite article
re means about, concerning
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: An American farmer, looking to buy, takes in an item about credit terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential buyer' sounds like an estate-agent phrase, but it is simply someone out shopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharecropper is a tenant farmer in the American South who pays rent with part of the crop.

clue.text: With court appearance a possibility, arranged bail at once

indicators.note: letters that are arranged are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Bail is set up immediately, as a court hearing may follow.
explanation.definitionFit: An actionable deed gives grounds for a lawsuit, so a court case could follow.

clue.text: Feeling of anxiety upset attempt to produce bridgelike structure

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a nag is a nagging worry or doubt
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Worry derails an effort to build something like a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A gantry is a raised bridge-like frame carrying signals or a crane.

clue.text: Aim to make sailor understand

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
to get something is to understand it

explanation.surface: A goal is to make a seaman grasp something.
explanation.definitionFit: A target is something aimed at, a synonym of aim as a noun.

clue.text: Fabric in vehicle particularly liked

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a pet is a favourite, as in pet project

explanation.surface: Upholstery inside a car is what someone especially likes.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpet is a thick woven textile, so a kind of fabric for floors.

clue.text: One finishing period of self-denial ignoring daughter's clasp, say?

parts.note: a fast is a time of going without food

indicators.note: ignoring a letter means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: an ender is one who ends something

explanation.surface: Someone breaking a fast forgets a daughter's brooch.
explanation.definitionFit: A clasp is one example of a fastener, hence the 'say' marking an example.

clue.text: Clever idea some linked with Star Trek broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast suggests something scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A television transmission connects some viewers to a famous sci-fi series.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterstroke is a brilliant, decisive move or idea.

clue.text: Unpleasant place man will be seen in

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
'll is the contracted form of will

explanation.surface: A man will be spotted somewhere grim.
explanation.walkthrough: HE plus 'LL makes the contraction for 'he will'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell is the place of torment, the archetypal unpleasant location.

clue.text: Ethnic group with dish in better frequented location?

parts.note: a race is a group sharing ethnic origin
a course is one dish of a meal

explanation.surface: A people with a meal that is in better spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is one who bets, not 'more good': a racecourse is where punters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Racecourses are where punters place bets on horses.

clue.text: Criminally, feed line extremes of bias can be justified by argument

indicators.note: criminally suggests the letters are treated wrongly and so reshuffled
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A biased line fed to the public is defended as justifiable.
explanation.walkthrough: FEED, LINE and the B and S of 'bias' are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensible position can be upheld with reasons, so it can be justified by argument.

clue.text: Resolve strain? One can, being broad-minded

indicators.note: to resolve something is to break it up and reform it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone tells another to settle a tension, since one is able to.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsectarian means not tied to any religious sect, hence tolerant and open.

clue.text: Be evasive over what's charged for horse?

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: to stall is to play for time, avoiding a straight answer
an ion is a particle that carries an electric charge

explanation.surface: Someone dodges the question of the price of a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse.

clue.text: Excite curiosity of characters from entire street

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of these words are taken and rearranged

explanation.surface: People are intrigued by figures from all along the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To interest someone is to arouse their curiosity, so the verb fits.

clue.text: Polite matron, refined, characteristic of London perhaps?

indicators.note: refined means processed and changed, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A courteous, cultured matron typifies the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Metropolitan means typical of a capital city, London being one example.

clue.text: Convincing air inspires leaders of the recruits

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one word takes in the others

parts.note: an air is a tune, a song

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A rousing tune motivates the heads of the new soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong argument is a convincing one, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Seem awed at first — extremely quiet on organ?

indicators.note: at first picks out the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Someone looks awestruck at very soft music played on an organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a church instrument, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to seem, as in 'he appears tired'.

clue.text: Printing expert terse and petty if messed about

indicators.note: letters messed about are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A typographer is curt and small-minded if mucked around.
explanation.definitionFit: A typesetter arranges type for printing, a skilled print trade.

clue.text: Faltered regularly in rush

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled repeatedly while hurrying.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away, rushing off from danger.

clue.text: Initially placate the French with first-class excuse

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the next word

parts.note: le is French for the
A, as in A1 or A grade, means first-class

explanation.surface: To soothe the French you need a top-rate excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea is a pleaded excuse or justification.

clue.text: Act assuming some won't come because of personal problem? All right

parts.note: over can mean because of, as in a row over money
BO, body odour, is a personal hygiene problem
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a private trouble is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'personal problem' looks like an emotional issue but is body odour.
explanation.definitionFit: Airlines and hotels overbook, taking more bookings than places, betting on no-shows.

clue.text: Revised clue is "It carries water"

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An edited crossword clue now reads as a statement about water.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluice is a channel with a gate controlling the flow of water.

clue.text: Open air worker — in forest in Germany?

indicators.note: this in places the forest within the abbreviation for Germany

parts.note: Arden is the English forest of Shakespeare's As You Like It

explanation.surface: Is an outdoor labourer working in a German forest?
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener tends plants outdoors, so works in the open air.

clue.text: Great attraction of publication associated with computers?

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a publication
the net, or internet, is the network of computers

explanation.surface: A computing magazine is a huge draw.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet is figuratively something or someone that strongly attracts people.
